arxiv-2201-11884.creator: A. Feder Cooper, Gili Vidan
arxiv-2201-11884.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. Feder Cooper, Gili Vidan. Contemporary concerns over the governance of technological systems often run up against narratives about the technical infeasibility of designing mechanisms for accountability. While in recent AI ethics literature these concerns have been deliberated predominantly in relation to machine learning, other instances in the history of computing also presented circumstances in which computer scientists needed to un-muddle what it means to design accountable systems.

arxiv-2302-12388.title: TrafFormer: A Transformer Model for Predicting Long-Term Traffic
arxiv-2302-12388.creator: David Alexander Tedjopurnomo, Farhana M. Choudhury, A. K. Qin
arxiv-2302-12388.description: Abstract Traffic prediction is a flourishing research field due to its importance in human mobility in the urban space. Despite this, existing studies only focus on short-term prediction of up to few hours in advance, with most being up to one hour only.

arxiv-2305-02834.creator: Gaëtan Fournier, Alberto Grillo, Yevgeny Tsodikovich
arxiv-2305-02834.description: Abstract We study candidates’ positioning when adjustments are possible in response to new information about voters’ preferences. Re-positioning allows candidates to get closer to the median voter but is costly both financially and electorally. We examine the occurrence and the direction of the adjustments depending on the ex-ante positions and the new information.

arxiv-2306-17259.title: Infomap Bioregions 2 - Exploring the interplay between biogeography and evolution
arxiv-2306-17259.creator: Daniel Edler, Anton Holmgren, Alexis Rojas, Joaquín Calatayud, Martin Rosvall, Alexandre Antonelli
arxiv-2306-17259.description: Abstract Identifying and understanding the large-scale biodiversity patterns in time and space is vital for conservation and addressing fundamental ecological and evolutionary questions. Network-based methods have proven useful for simplifying and highlighting important structures in species distribution data. However, current network-based biogeography approaches cannot exploit the evolutionary information available in phylogenetic data.

arxiv-2307-03372.title: Triangle singularity in the J / ψ → γ ​ p ¯ ​ Δ J/\psi\to\gamma\bar{p}\Delta decay
arxiv-2307-03372.creator: Ke Wang, Rong Li, Bo-Chao Liu
arxiv-2307-03372.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ke Wang, Rong Li, Bo-Chao Liu. In this work, we study the role of triangle singularity in the J / ψ → γ ​ p ¯ ​ Δ J/\psi\to\gamma\bar{p}\Delta decay. We find that through a triangle mechanism, involving a triangle loop composed by ω \omega , π \pi and p p , this decay may develop a triangle singularity and produce a visible peak in the invariant mass M γ ​ Δ M_{\gamma\Delta} around 1.73 GeV with a width of 0.02 GeV.

arxiv-2404-04711.title: On the Uniqueness and Orbital Stability of Slow and Fast Solitary Wave Solutions of the Benjamin Equation
arxiv-2404-04711.creator: May ABDALLAH, Mohamad DARWICH, Luc MOLINET
arxiv-2404-04711.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by May ABDALLAH, Mohamad DARWICH, Luc MOLINET. This paper is devoted to the study of existence and properties of solitary waves of the Benjamin equation. The studied equation includes a parameter γ \gamma in front of the Benjamin-Ono term. We show the existence, uniqueness, decay and orbital stability of solitary wave solutions obtained as a solution to a certain minimization problem, associated either with high speeds without a sign condition on the parameter γ \gamma or with low speeds for the appropriate sign.

arxiv-2512-18761.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dimitrios Tyrovolas, Sotiris A. Tegos, Yue Xiao. Programmable wireless environments (PWEs) have emerged as a key paradigm for next-generation communication networks, aiming to transform wireless propagation from an uncontrollable phenomenon into a reconfigurable process that can adapt to diverse service requirements. In this framework, pinching-antenna systems (PASs) have recently been proposed as a promising enabling technology, as they allow the radiation location and effective propagation distance to be adjusted by selectively exciting radiating points along a dielectric waveguide.

arxiv-2601-07065.title: FormulaCompiler.jl and Margins.jl: Efficient Marginal Effects in Julia
arxiv-2601-07065.creator: Eric Feltham
arxiv-2601-07065.description: Abstract Marginal effects analysis is fundamental to interpreting statistical models, yet existing implementations face computational constraints that limit analysis at scale. We introduce two Julia packages that address this gap. Margins.jl provides a clean two-function API organizing analysis around a 2 × 2 2\times 2 framework: evaluation context (population vs profile) by analytical target (effects vs predictions).
